newsitem.title: UK: FEATURE - Pfandbrief market widens horizons.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Pfandbrief market widens horizons.

text.p: Germany's Pfandbrief bond market is estimated to be the fifth largest bond sector in the world but until recently has also been one of the world's most introspective markets.
Now all that is changing.

The Pfandbrief, a German bond issued by authorised banks to refinance mortgages or public projects, has been mostly unrated by the major credit rating agencies and bought mainly by domestic investors.

But as this market strives to attract a broader base of investment, it is coming under pressure to solicit ratings. Many international investors are prohibited from buying unrated paper regardless of the perceived asset quality.

"One year ago, ratings were relatively unimportant. Now international investors are very keen to have ratings (on Pfandbrief)," Frankfurter Hypothekenbank Centralboden board member Bernd Knobloch said at a meeting of Pfandbrief market players.
It is also considered essential in a post-European economic and monetary union (EMU) environment in which ratings will be the main guideline for investment.
The pressure on the Pfandbrief sector has come about partly by its own ambition.
The development of a jumbo Pfandbrief, the global Pfandbrief and most recently the Euro-Asian Pfandbrief has raised the sector's profile.
Other key advances have been Pfandbrief electronic trading systems and new indices tracking the price and performance of the Pfandbrief - the PEX and PEXP respectively.
CONFLICTING VIEWS ON HOW TO RATE PFANDBRIEF BONDS

In July, Moody's Investors Service said the probability of default between the German Pfandbrief and an underlying issuing bank could not be separated. It said German mortgage banks could be vulnerable to the penalties of bankcruptcy or to the imposition of regulators' emergency measures.
But Pfandbrief devotee Walter Dieck, president of the Association of German Mortgage Banks, attacked this idea.
"No issuer had ever defaulted. The security of the Pfandbrief is unsurpassed in Germany," he said at the meeting in London.
Dieck said the association had advocated a "system rating" for the sector some years ago, with the idea being that one Pfandbrief was as good as another. But the rating agencies decided against that.
"If it were up to the rating agencies they would rate the some 16,000 Pfandbrief issues individually," Dieck said.
Meanwhile Moody's senior analyst Tobias Grun said at the conference it was important that the Pfandbrief were rated.
"Mortgage banks are exposed to banking risks...they have the capability of going bankcrupt... We see a link between Pfandbrief performance and the credit-worthiness of the underlying issuer."
STANDARD AND POOR'S DEVELOPING OWN CRITIERIA FOR PFANDBRIEFE
Standard & Poor's said it had developed new criteria for rating Pfandbrief which allowed the bonds to exceed the banks' counterparty ratings.
"Their collateral, coupled with protections afforded by German insolvency and banking laws, permit S&P to rate some Pfandbriefe above the bank's counterparty rating.

"Although such institutions are subject to the risk of failure, S&P believes that holders of some Pfandbriefe, especially those backed by public sector loans, may continue to receive full and timely payments in the event of the bank's insolvency."

S&P director and head of structured finance Kurt Sampson, also speaking at the Pfandbrief meeting, said: "We do believe that the financial condition of the institution itself is of much less importance than the quality of the collateral."
He said it would be possible for a bank's Pfandbrief bonds to be rated higher than the issuer itself.

Individual Pfandbrief are all secured against a large, separately registered pool of loans to the public sector -- in the case of public Pfandbriefe -- or of first mortgages on residential and commercial property as in the case of Mortgage Pfandbriefe.
SOME RATINGS ALREADY EXIST
In 1987 Pfandbrief issued by Frankfurter Hypothekenbank AG were rated AAA by Standard & Poor's Corp.

Recently, Moody's assigned a AAA rating to Depfa Bank's (Deutsche Pfandbrief- und Hypothekenbank AG) public Pfandbriefe and Aa1 to its mortgage Pfandbriefe. It awarded a AAA rating to both the public and mortgage Pfandbriefe issued by Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and RHEINHYP (Rheinische Hypothekenbank AG).
New issue activity in the Pfandbrief market exploded following German reunification in 1990 and the boom in demand for public-sector commercial and residential loans which accompanied it.
"There remains a tremendous potential for catching up in housing construction in former East Germany," said Dieke.

Outstanding Pfandbrief total about 1.4 trillion marks ($897 billion), representing more than one-third of the German bond market. It is more than twice the size of the British government bond "gilt" market.
